cards.explanation: The answer is what people will be like. Paul doesn't point at the weather or the headlines. He points at people, and then the list rolls in: "…lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant…" (2 Timothy 3:2). I think that's Paul saying the trouble starts in the heart. Friends, he puts the whole mess on what people are like, and that's where he keeps his eyes.

The answer is to turn away from them. Paul says it short and sharp: "Turn away from such as these!" (2 Timothy 3:5). No long meeting, no group chat about it. When a box is all bow and no cookies, you set it down and walk away. Paul gives Timothy a clear instruction and doesn't dress it up.

The catch is that they never come to know the truth. Paul says they are "…always learning but never able to come to a knowledge of the truth." (2 Timothy 3:7). It's like driving laps around the block, learning every street and never pulling into the driveway. All that learning, and the truth never lands, friends. Paul names that gap and doesn't soften it.

The answer is depraved. Paul says these men "…are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith." (2 Timothy 3:8). It's a heavy word, and he means it. Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, and Paul says these men oppose the truth in the same way. Paul keeps it plain.

The answer is True. Paul says these men "…are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith." (2 Timothy 3:8). He says it right after saying they oppose the truth. It's a serious line, friends, and Paul states it plainly.
The answer is False. Paul says, "But they will not advance much further." (2 Timothy 3:9). These men have a limit. They're not climbing forever, friends, and Paul says so right there in the verse.

The answer is plain. Paul says "…their folly will be plain to everyone." (2 Timothy 3:9). He says it will be plain, just like it was with Jannes and Jambres. Everyone will see it, friends. That's the kind of ending that makes me smile.
